business_problem: To better reach students from all backgrounds, George Mason University aimed to create a more efficient, student-centered experience with data and automation. Mason used dashboards for real-time goal tracking and behavior-based models to scale up recruitment.
solution_summary: George Mason University used Salesforce to replace fragmented student-support processes and low-scale recruiting workflows with a more automated, student-centered operating model. Service Cloud became the one-stop case and history layer for student services, replacing four separate offices and giving staff access to each student's prior issues and current context so questions about registration, enrollment, and financial aid can be handled in one place. Tableau and CRM Analytics provide real-time visibility into recruitment goals, behavior-based models, and emerging service bottlenecks, allowing the university to monitor territory performance, direct resources to problem areas, and spot students who need help even if they never reach out. The result is a single data-driven support and recruitment stack that lets recruiters scale from hundreds of contacts to thousands while improving issue resolution and student satisfaction without a comparable increase in staffing.
